cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Apologize Properly
cards.instruction: Get someone to deliver the apology in the form, order, and setting you consider valid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Your apology email needs a subject line mentioning the broken vase.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. For all I know, that's about your choice of font.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send 'Sorry about the vase' to Mum. She still thinks you broke it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with 'I broke it.' My name comes out of the story before your apology goes in.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 edits the subject and A5 sets confession order, so form control is present; A3 generic rank prefix does little beyond the ordinary demand for a specific apology.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 sorry subject causes A3 ambiguity objection; B4 Mum blaming A causes A5 personal confession before apology.

relationship.evidence: B2 supplies existing wording and B4 proposes a fix with new audience stakes, materially changing what the email must establish.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 mistaken blame to escalate from subject specificity to authorship of damage, preserving the apology task.

specificity.evidence: A1 broken vase email and B4 Mum misunderstanding establish clear family communication without needing identities.
